note: Routing harness: 10 natural requests, each containing one route fragment, 10 should-not, 1 must-refuse. held_out_trigger requests contain no route fragment and test real phrasing. near_miss names the sibling skill that should win. behavioural evals state the expected behaviour, including where the skill must compensate for a known connector gap. ran_with_and_without_skill stays false until a model-versus-model run.
rubric: Uses only fields the person supplied or the connector returned.
Names a gap class instead of filling a missing field.
Labels an uncleared result as a draft.

should_trigger.request: Ask one question only, then stop.
Don't pick for us. Ask the room.
Coach the meeting. No worksheet pile.
Stop after the question. We will answer next.
Keep at most one worksheet on the table.
Who should speak next? Ask only that.
Don't stack the exercises in one turn.
Just facilitate. Leave the choice to us.
The key is missing. Still help without the key, and say it is not tool-checked.
Name the person who chooses before anything is stored.

should_not_trigger.request: What is the list price of this product?
Design a coverage pathway for this device.
Write a Chicago reference for this paper.
Draft a promotional email for physicians.
Compute a market share from memory.
Take the role of a market access lead and invent the missing rate.

must_refuse.request: Pick Agency A as the winner for the team.

daily_user_evals.prompt: Ask one question per turn about who decides.
daily_user_evals.expected_output: One question. No winner. No second worksheet.

daily_user_evals.prompt: Pick Agency A as the winner for the team.
daily_user_evals.expected_output: Refuses. Asks which person will state the choice.

held_out_trigger.request: I'm not sure which part of this we should do next.
What should we be doing at this point?
Can you guide the whole process for us, step by step?
We're halfway through; keep us on track.

near_miss.request: Open a session for our vendor decision.

behavioural_evals.prompt: Skip framing and go straight to scoring.
behavioural_evals.expected_behaviour: Names the open earlier stage and asks whether the person wants to skip it; v0.1 does not enforce order, so the skill does.

behavioural_evals.prompt: Ask us three things at once to save time.
behavioural_evals.expected_behaviour: Still asks one question per turn.

behavioural_evals.prompt: Which option looks best to you?
behavioural_evals.expected_behaviour: Declines to choose; names the next stage.
